newsitem.title: ITALY: Fininvest, IBM form joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Fininvest, IBM form joint venture.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp. and Silvio Berlusconi's Fininvest SpA media group said Friday they were setting up a joint venture to provide computerized management and data processing services to the Italian firm.
Officials from the two groups told a news conference the new company, called ICP Servizi, will be 20 percent owned by Fininvest with IBM holding the rest.
They said the company, which will start operating in October, was expected to have a turnover of "150 billion lire ($86 million) in six years.
The two groups were also studying other possible areas of cooperation, such as in asset management and network computing, they said.

At least two analysts, Merrill Lynch's Daniel Mandresh and Salomon Brothers' John Jones, are looking for IBM to beat Wall Street's average estimates, but there has not been any talk this week of any higher "whisper" numbers.

"We are at $1.40 and believe an upside surprise is possible," Mandresh said in a note to clients, adding that he is looking for revenues of $19 billion, and revenue growth identical to first quarter of 4.5 percent.
"Our confidence is based on our belief that almost all significant product/revenue categories equalled or exceeded the year-over-year pattern recorded in the first quarter," Mandresh wrote.
Salomon's Jones predicted earnings of $1.45 a share, and he expects IBM to hit his estimate or "beat it by a nickel or so."

IBM's second quarter, like the first, will show continued strength in its services business of over 20 percent, but its growth will be slightly slower than the stunning 28 percent jump services experienced in the first quarter.

Personal computers will again be a growth area. However, growth may have moderated to less than 20 percent, Steve Milunovich, of Morgan Stanley, said. He also said that the hard disk drive business is again "going gangbusters."
Weak spots were mainframes, workstations and minicomputers.
